memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses said, 'Now show me your glory.'" - Exod 33:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four words, and they change the temperature of the whole chapter.

Moses has received everything he asked for. God's presence is promised. Rest is granted. The people are spared. He could have stopped there, satisfied. Instead he asks for more — not more blessing, but more of God.

That is the mark of a heart truly alive to God. Every answered prayer only deepens the appetite. Those who know God best are always the hungriest for Him.

Compare this with our usual praying. We ask God for help, for healing, for provision, for guidance — all good and right. But how often do we simply say, "Show me Your glory"? How often do we want God for God's sake, and not for what He can arrange for us?

Here is the wonder of the gospel. What Moses asked to see, we have been given in Christ. "We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son" (John 1:14). God's glory has a human face — the face of Jesus Christ (2 Cor 4:6).

Moses asked on a mountain and was shown a glimpse. We hold the Gospels in our hands and see the Son. Do we hunger for Him as Moses did?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you want God's gifts more than God Himself?
2. When did you last ask God simply to reveal Himself to you?
3. How can you seek God's glory in the face of Christ this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, show me Your glory. Not just Your help — I want more of You. Amen.
